content.comment_body: I am using a [product_name] standard module with an 8-position [product_name] expansion card. The program downloads successfully. I have several switches wired with 24VDC control voltage to the [product_name] inputs, some are maintained and some are momentary. However, the [product_name] is not detecting any inputs. Diagnostics in [product_name] engineering software only mention 'no SD card.' Any recommendations?
What color does the LED display on the expansion module? Is it red, yellow, or green?
The LED shows green, the unit is in Run mode, and I can access the online test function.
Hello, It could be an electrical problem. Can you provide a photo showing your wiring setup? Also, did you use a handheld multimeter to confirm the voltage supplied to the [product_name]?

The wiring is direct. I use a 24VDC power supply, with 24VDC connected to the top of each switch and the bottom to the [product_name] input. When the switch is off, there is no 24V measured between input and negative terminal. When it's on, I measure 24V between the input and the negative terminal. The [product_name] runs on 120VAC, which is operating normally. Circuit continuity is confirmed, and 24V is present at terminals when the power supply is on.
With the [product_name] 230VAC version, you cannot use 24VDC on the inputs—only 115-230VAC input voltage is supported.
I have a [product_name] 230RCE model that runs on 120VAC. It is labeled 'input 8x AC/DC.' Are you suggesting the input control voltage must be 120VAC for this model?
I can't recall all the specifications—did you receive an information pamphlet with the hardware? Checking those specifications could help.
For precise specifications, please review the attached document.
Thank you all for your help. It seems I need to modify the wiring setup. Have a great weekend.
Wishing you a great weekend as well.

analysis.insight_summary: The user experienced difficulties with a [product_name] and its expansion module not detecting input signals provided via switches using 24VDC, revealing confusion about correct input voltage requirements for different module versions. Diagnostic tools did not highlight wiring errors, and the issue was traced to an incompatibility between the used control voltage and required input voltage for the hardware. This points to the importance of clear hardware specifications communication.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipated that the [product_name] would recognize 24VDC signals at the inputs, assuming compatibility with their chosen control voltage. They also expected diagnostic features to help pinpoint connectivity or configuration issues for easier troubleshooting.
